title: “PUT YOUR HAND HERE.”
paragraphs: The room went silent when Jesus said it.

Not to Peter.
Not to John.
To the one disciple everyone whispered about.
The Moment Doubt Met the Wounds
Thomas had drawn a line in the sand.
“Unless I see the nail marks in His hands and put my finger where the nails were, and put my hand into His side, I will not believe.” — Gospel of John 20:25

Eight days passed.
Eight long days of stubborn unbelief.

The locked room.
The trembling disciples.
And Jesus standing there again.
Closer than anyone else in that room.

The one who demanded proof
was the one Jesus offered His wounds.
They were the evidence of love.
Thomas touched the place where the spear had torn flesh.
The place where blood and water once flowed.
And in that moment the doubter collapsed into worship.
“My Lord and my God!” — Gospel of John 20:28
The Gospel Hidden in the Scars

The nails.
The spear.
The cross.
All of it because sin demanded justice.
“He was pierced for our transgressions.” — Book of Isaiah 53:5
The scars of Christ are the receipts of redemption.
Proof that the debt was paid.
And Then Jesus Said Something For Us
“Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed.” — Gospel of John 20:29

Doubt can become worship
when it touches the scars of Christ.
Jesus is not afraid of honest doubt.
He answers it with nail-scarred hands.
We tell the stories shame tried to erase.
